Package hadur2.core.memory

Class ProfileCodec

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.memory.ProfileCodec
public final class ProfileCodec extends Object
The profile file format: small, hand-written, versioned and checksummed (the artifact's "Format" section). Not Java serialisation, which breaks when classes change, and not text, which would not fit many opponents in the 200 KB data quota. 
 'H' 'P'           magic
 u8                version (2; version 1 still loads)
 i32               payload length
 payload           see encode(hadur2.core.memory.OpponentProfile)
 i32               CRC-32 of everything before it

decode(byte[]) either returns a profile whose every count is finite and not negative, or throws ProfileFormatException; no input, however damaged, makes it throw anything else (MEM-4). A file from an unknown version is rejected like a damaged one, so the opponent is treated as a stranger rather than misread.

The checksum is what makes RES-3's write order safe: a file cut short at any byte either fails the length check or the CRC, so ProfileLibrary can always tell a complete copy from a torn one. Every count read back is also checked to be finite and not negative, and every list length against its cap, so even a file with a valid CRC but nonsense values cannot put a NaN or an unbounded list into the core (RES-2).

Encoding is deterministic: the same profile always gives the same bytes.

    • VERSION

      public static final int VERSION
      2 adds the normalised hit counts after the motion group (S4) and gives the seeds their meaning (Seeds). A version 1 file loads with those counts at zero and without its seeds, which had no defined layout (S3 never filled them): stats kept, seeds dropped.

  • Method Details

    • encode

      public static byte[] encode(OpponentProfile p)
      Encodes a profile in the current VERSION. The payload holds, in order:
      1. key and last name (u8 length, then UTF-16 units); battles and rounds (i32); lastFought (i64);
      2. the outcomes: a u8 count, then rounds and wins (u16) and our and their damage (f32) for each;
      3. the count groups, each a u8 length and f32 values: shots at us, hits on us, shots and hits by motion, the power histogram, virtual waves and hits, our shots and hits, motion, and (version 2) the normalised waves and hits;
      4. the gun seed, then the surf seed: a u16 count, a u8 width (13), then the samples' shorts.
      Parameters:
      p - the profile
      Returns:
      the file's bytes, header, payload and CRC included

    • encode

      public static byte[] encode(OpponentProfile p, int version)
      MEM-7: encodes a profile in version instead of the current one, so a client still running a previous release can go on reading what a newer one writes. Only OLDEST_VERSION to VERSION are supported, the same range decode(byte[]) accepts; a version-gated field a target version does not have (today, only the normalised-hits group, added in version 2) is left out, exactly as that version's own encoder would have left it out.
      Parameters:
      p - the profile
      version - the format version to write, OLDEST_VERSION to VERSION
      Returns:
      the file's bytes, header, payload and CRC included
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if version is outside the supported range

    • encodeStatsOnly

      static byte[] encodeStatsOnly(OpponentProfile p)
      TIME-4: encodes p's statistics with empty seed sections, without ever serialising its actual (possibly large, capped-size) seed lists. Used to build a cheap, independent copy of just the stats fields for a checkpoint that will not write seeds; the copy still decodes at the current version, so seeds carried over from elsewhere can be added back onto it afterwards.
      Parameters:
      p - the profile
      Returns:
      the file's bytes, header, payload and CRC included, with no seed samples

    • decode

      public static OpponentProfile decode(byte[] bytes)
      Decodes a profile written by encode(hadur2.core.memory.OpponentProfile), in this version or any since OLDEST_VERSION.
      Parameters:
      bytes - the file's content; may be null
      Returns:
      a profile whose every count is finite and not negative and whose lists are within their caps
      Throws:
      ProfileFormatException - for any input that is not such a profile; no other exception escapes (MEM-4)
